chief_data.selection_justification: Selected Candidate 4 as the only viable flow design that meets safety hard gates (BPR > ΔP) and achieves the required 3.0x residence-time reduction (τ=23.7 min vs batch ~70+ min implied by kinetics) while maintaining high conversion (0.85). Candidates 2 and 3 were disqualified due to critical pressure drop violations (ΔP >> BPR limit). Candidate 1 was rejected due to lower conversion (0.70) and higher mixing resistance compared to Candidate 4. Warning: no concrete flow advantage identified. This design may not justify flow over batch.
chief_data.selection_rationale: Candidate 4 is selected as the winner with a combined score of 0.758, significantly outperforming Candidate 1 (0.718). The primary driver for Candidate 4's superiority is its higher conversion (0.85 vs 0.70) and better fluidic performance (lower r_mix 0.099 vs 0.159), which is critical for the selectivity-sensitive Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution mechanism. Candidates 2 and 3 were disqualified because their pressure drops (723 bar and 2901 bar respectively) vastly exceeded the Back Pressure Regulator limit of 1.5 bar, creating an immediate safety and feasibility failure. Candidate 1, while feasible, suffered from insufficient conversion and poorer mixing characteristics, failing to fully leverage the flow advantage for selectivity. The user objective of 'balanced' performance favored Candidate 4's robust safety margin and high yield over Candidate 1's marginal performance. The most significant remaining uncertainty is the exact kinetic enhancement factor in flow versus batch, as the model assumes ideal plug flow behavior. The first experiment on the bench should verify the conversion at τ=23.7 min and check for any fouling or precipitation in the 0.75 mm channel at 60°C.
resolved_tradeoffs: id=4 vs id=1: id=4 has higher conversion (0.85 vs 0.70) and better mixing (r_mix 0.099 vs 0.159), justifying the slightly longer residence time (23.7 vs 14.7 min) for superior selectivity and yield.
id=2 and id=3 disqualified: ΔP (723 bar and 2901 bar) exceeds BPR limit (1.5 bar) by orders of magnitude, violating hard safety gates.
remaining_uncertainties: Kinetic rate constant k may vary in flow due to enhanced mass transfer; current model assumes batch-derived k.
Potential for fouling in 0.75 mm channels at 60°C over long runs is not modeled.
chief_data.experiment_recommendation: Run reaction at Q=0.447 mL/min, T=60°C, τ=23.7 min. Monitor conversion and selectivity. Check for pressure stability and channel fouling after 2 hours.
